newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soyoil ends higher, meal mostly lower.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soyoil ends higher, meal mostly lower.

text.p: CBOT soyoil futures closed firmer on Thursday while soymeal contracts were mostly lower amid talk China had bought U.S. soy products, traders said.
"China has been pretty active," said Ron Kucha of O'Connor and Co. "There is some business being done."
Soymeal futures turned weak in late dealings in line with a slide in wheat futures, traders said.

But soyoil remained firm after commercial buying in the soyoil pit sparked an early rally and stops were hit, traders said. ADM Investor Services reportedly was a buyer which prompted fund buying interest, they said.
Traders speculated the commercial buying was tied to export business. There was talk China had bought 20,000 tonnes U.S. soyoil and up to 75,000 tonnes soymeal.
But export sources discounted the China rumors, saying China had bought soyoil earlier in the week but there had been no additional business.
Soyoil closed up 0.12 to 0.04 cent per lb with December up 0.08 at 23.16. Soymeal closed down $1.50 to $0.10 per ton with December down $1.20 at $231.30.
ADM Investor Services, Cargill Inc, Central Soya, Produce Grain and Continental Grain sold soymeal, traders said.
Refco Inc sold at least 150 lots January soymeal while Smith Barney bought 150 lots March, traders said.
ADM Investor Services was also a seller of 150 lots of March soyoil but a small-lot buyer of the December, traders said. Produce Grain bought December and January soyoil late.
Smith Barney reportedly sold at least 150 lots December but bought 250 lots, traders said.

Crush margins were weaker on the day with November/ December down 0.26 cent per bushel to 72.37 cents and January off 0.61 cent to 59.75. But cash soymeal brokers anticipated a third straight week of record high crushing levels.
They estimated the National Oilseed Processors Association weekly crush, due this afternoon, at 29.20 million to 31.00 million bushels. Last week's crush was 29.90 million bushels.
